pages.text: Decelerators decelerate particles to lower energy. This is useful for creating things like neutral antimatter in an $(l:multiblocks/vacuum_chambers/exotic_containment_chamber)exotic containment chamber$(/l) or just to lower particle energy to a certain amount.

pages.title: Construction
pages.text: Decelerators are built like $(l:multiblocks/accelerators/ring_accelerator#construction)Ring Accelerators$(/l). The notable differences are that they cannot have Accelerator Synchrotron Ports and gain no benefit from more than one RF Cavity.

pages.title: Operation
pages.text: A Decelerator functions like a $(l:multiblocks/accelerators/ring_accelerator#operation)Ring Accelerator$(/l). Its maximum input particle energy is $(br)$(l)Eᵩ=(qB₂R)²/(2m)$(), the same dipole-strength limit used for a $(l:multiblocks/accelerators/ring_accelerator#max_dipole)Ring Accelerator's$(/l) output.

The energy of the output particles is determined by the strength of the redstone signal applied to the controller (or input $(l:multiblocks/accelerators/general#redstone)redstone port$(/l)). A full 15 strength will decelerate down to < 1 keV, effectivly zero. This is required for creating neutral antimatter. For any redstone strength, the energy the decelerator will try to output the particles at is $(br)$(l)E=Eᵩ(1-Sᵣ/15)$() where $(l)Sᵣ$() is the redstone signal strength.

For example, if we have a decelerator with a max input energy of 2 GeV and we apply a redstone signal of 8, then $(br)2 GeV*(1-8/15)=933.33 MeV. $(br2)$(bold)Note:$() If the inputted particle energy is lower than this targeted energy it will leave the energy unchanged (i.e. it does not increase particle energy).

As with Ring Accelerators, server integrations can control output percentage through the $(l:multiblocks/open_computers/introduction#accelerator_control)common server-side API$(/l). OpenComputers peripherals are not reintroduced.
